I have resolved the issue in [related_descriptors.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1wv5ii6d/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py).

### Cause
When prefetching related objects via [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1wv5ii6d/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1wv5ii6d/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L365-L382), or `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`'s [`RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1wv5ii6d/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L633-L654), iterating over `queryset` evaluates any nested `prefetch_related()` / `select_related()` lookups on the related objects first, populating their relation caches. Afterward, the loop body unconditionally assigned the outer `instance` to the reverse relation cache on each `rel_obj`, overwriting the inner prefetched instance (and its loaded/deferred fields) with the outer parent instance.

### Fix
Check `is_cached(rel_obj)` on the corresponding field/relation before caching `instance` on `rel_obj` in:
- [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1wv5ii6d/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L145-L149)
- [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1wv5ii6d/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L379-L382)
- [`RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1wv5ii6d/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L650-L653)
